name: Map
grades: A: no errors and at most 1 warning. B: no errors. C: 1 error. D: 2 errors. F: 3 or more. Each rule counts once, however many places it fires. Hints never count.

1.name: Map fills the width and most of the height

2.name: Pins or icons on the map

3.name: Card, sheet or panel docked at the bottom

4.name: Floating button or pill over the map

5.name: Time, date, wait or opening hours shown

7.name: Search field or place field at the top

9.name: Button in the panel or floating at the bottom

10.name: Chips or filter pills over the map

v1.name: Pins and place card
v1.lead: Pins, often with a place card
expect: Pins or icons mark places on the map, from a few to a crowd
A card or sheet for the selected place is docked at the bottom on most screens
Floating buttons or pills sit over the map, mostly in the top third
A locate arrow floats on the map on most screens

v2.name: Map with one action
expect: A button for the one action sits at the bottom, in a panel or floating
A pin or icons on the map, mostly in the upper part
Floating buttons at the top of the map, such as back or close
No tab bar and no search field: the map and one button carry the screen

v4.name: Small map above list
v4.lead: Small map above a form or list
expect: The map is a frame that takes about a third of the height, in the upper part
Fields or a list below the map fill most of the rest of the screen
Pins or a marker sit on the small map on most screens

not_checked: What happens after a tap on a pin, the map or a button: one screen cannot show it.
Pins that crowd on a map with only a few of them: the pin rule counts pins, it does not measure overlap.
Dim street names on a dark map are judged by a reader, because the map labels are not parts the script measures.

rules.says: So many pins sit on the map that they bunch up, cover each other and hide the map names.
rules.why: Pins crowd and overlap their labels in dense areas. Seen on 31 of 60 checked screens.

rules.says: A permission dialog sits over the map and hides it until the person acts.
rules.why: A permission dialog sits over the map and hides it until the person acts. Seen on 1 of 60 checked screens.

rules.says: On a dark map the street names are small and dim grey, and the dots between them are hard to tell apart.
rules.why: On the dark maps the street labels are small and dim, and the purple dots on Check sit among them. Seen on 5 of 60 checked screens.

rules.says: Text or a close control is too faint against what is behind it.
rules.why: Accessibility guidelines ask for 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text: 18 pt, or 14 pt bold (button labels are bold). Controls, such as a close or back glyph, need 3:1. Below 3:1 is an error; from 3:1 to 4.5:1 on smaller text it is a warning. Checked on the labels of buttons, the lines of the parts marked as key text, and the close and back glyphs. Not checked on a dimmed screen or over a photo or a pattern, or on the label of a greyed-out button (the guidelines leave out controls that cannot be used yet). Faint placeholder text in an empty field is only a hint, since iOS's own placeholder grey is about 1.7:1.

rules.says: Text is smaller than 11 pt.
rules.why: Apple lists 11 pt as the smallest text size on iOS. Measured from the height of each line, so it is about right, not exact. Checked on the parts marked as key text.

rules.says: A control sits under the status bar or the home indicator.
rules.why: The status bar row at the top and the bottom 34 pt, where the home indicator sits, belong to the system on phones without a home button. Flagged when a control reaches the status bar row or comes within 17 pt of the bottom edge, so a button that only touches the area is not counted.

rules.says: A close or back control is drawn smaller than 13 pt.
rules.why: Apple asks for a 44 x 44 pt tap area. The standard close X in a bar is drawn about 13 to 17 pt across inside that area, so only a smaller drawing is flagged. A screenshot cannot show the tap area itself, so this is a hint.
